reason: A spurlike mentum, sac or short shoot has the shape of a small projecting spur: PATO:0002540 spur shaped.

label: flagelliform
definition: A linear quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being long, slender and flexible, tapering like a whip. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO setaceous; PATO:0104351 filiform is thread-like and not tapering.
reason: Whiplike shoots, stolons and leaf tips are the standard botanical flagelliform; filiform (thread-like) is the nearest PATO term but misses the long, tapering, flexible sense.
'Without bristles' = not covered with bristles: negation of PATO:0002289 setose. Absence of trichome would be too broad, since it would mean glabrous.
A compound of two shape values that both have terms; it is written as a continuum, like linear-lanceolate.
A compound of two shape values, triangular with rounded corners; 'rounded' is read as obtuse, as in the accepted union pair 'rounded or capitate'.
An ecological or behavioural remark (growing in disturbed ground, spreading readily), not a quality of the plant's form.
A vague 'poorly developed' that can mean smaller, fewer-flowered or reduced depending on context; no single quality fits.

target: new: shape with oblique modifier (rectangular PATO_0001867 and asymmetrical PATO_0000616)
reason: Both values hold at once: a rectangular outline whose sides are unequal. 'Oblique' leaflets map to asymmetrical, as the rule for inequilateral does. This is an intersection, not a continuum.

reason: A region (the base of the blade or leaflet) plus a shape value; the region slot gives the base bearer, and 'rounded' is obtuse.

label: fine-grained
definition: A texture quality inhering in wood by virtue of its cells and vessels being small and closely and evenly spaced, so that its cut surface is even and fine. NOTE: Botany-specific (wood texture); coarse-grained is the opposite.
reason: A standard wood texture character in English and French floras; no PATO texture term covers it.
Flowerless branches, shoots and lower inflorescence axes have no flowers: complement of has_part some flower. 'In the lower 3-30 mm' goes to the region slot.
A comparison of two dimensions of one bearer (height > width), the pattern for 'longer than wide'.
Marine herbs live in sea water, a kind of aquatic; the salinity is a habitat detail outside PATO's scope, as noted for aquatic.
'Sheath: vague' means nothing as a quality. The other examples are 'vaginate/vaginées', which should get its own rule to FLOPO:0991105 sheathing rather than come in under this word.
A misspelling of laciniate (French laciniés); the 'lacérés' example is lacerate, FLOPO:0991115.
Meaningless without context ('capsule definite', 'stem definite'); it may mean determinate, distinct or a fixed number.
In-rolled margins and blades are rolled inwards: PATO:0001962 involute.
Ovulate cones are female (seed) cones, as pistillate maps to female; numbered forms ('3-7-ovulate', '∞-ovulées') belong to the count-of-parts pattern.
Ring-like arils, stigmas and sheaths: PATO:0002539 ring shaped (EXACT synonym annular).
A growth rate is a quality of a process, not of the plant's structure; putting PATO:0000912 increased rate on a whole plant would fall under the process-quality GCI and make the class unsatisfiable.

reason: The thinness is a quality of the shell (the pericarp of a nut, the seed coat), a part of the bearer named in the word.

A loose habit likeness (tall, cane-like grass habit) with no defined quality.

Mammiform = shaped like a nipple; PATO:0002108 papillary is resembling a small nipple-like projection.
